summary: The letters קהת form no verb or common noun in scripture: only the name קְהָת Kohath, Levi’s second son, and the gentilic קְהָתִי “Kohathite”, which with the article names his descendants as a clan, the Levites who carried “the holy things” of the sanctuary on the shoulder (Num 4:15; 7:9; 10:21). Scripture gives no reason for the name. It may be formed like יִקְּהָה “obedience” (Gen 49:10; Pro 30:17) with the first letter dropped, as Sabaean does with its noun qht “obedience; command” from the verb wqh “obey, command”; but this is a possibility, not shown.

words.summary: The gentilic of the name קְהָת, always with the article (fifteen uses): “the Kohathite”, singular for the clan as one, or plural הַקְּהָתִים. It means only “of Kohath”, so no cognate bears on it; what the name itself may mean is in the name entry. Its link to any wider sense of the root is not known.

senses.definition: Of Kohath: the descendants of Kohath son of Levi counted as a clan, in the phrase “the clan(s) of the Kohathite”, beside the Gershonite and the Merarite; the Amramite, Izharite, Hebronite and Uzzielite clans are its branches, and Aaron’s sons the priests are of it.

evidence.note: וְלִקְהָת מִשְׁפַּחַת הַעַמְרָמִי … אֵלֶּה הֵם מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַקְּהָתִי: the clans of Kohath’s four sons are “the clans of the Kohathite”.
לִקְהָת מִשְׁפַּחַת הַקְּהָתִי: “of Kohath, the clan of the Kohathite”, between the Gershonite and the Merarite: the gentilic is formed from the father’s name.
The prince of the father’s house of the clans of the Kohathite is Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
The counted of the clans of the Kohathite, all who served in the tent of meeting.
The lot came out for the clans of the Kohathite, “and the sons of Aaron the priest, of the Levites” had thirteen cities: the priests are Kohathites.
“For the sons of Aaron, of the clans of the Kohathite, of the sons of Levi, for theirs was the first lot.”
The same allotment in Chronicles: to the sons of Aaron, of the clan of the Kohathite.

senses.definition: With the article, alone or after בְּנֵי, the Kohathites as one company of Levites with their own service: carrying the holy things on the march, later the showbread, song and oversight of the house of God.

evidence.note: וְנָסְעוּ הַקְּהָתִים נֹשְׂאֵי הַמִּקְדָּשׁ: “the Kohathites set out, carrying the sanctuary”, after Reuben’s standard, and the Dwelling was set up before they came.
“Do not cut off שֵׁבֶט מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַקְּהָתִי from among the Levites”: the Kohathites as one tribe-like body, at risk because they carry the most holy things (4:19–20).
Moses, Aaron and the princes count בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִי by clans and fathers’ houses.
Of the sons of the Kohathite stood Heman the singer, son of Joel, son of Samuel.
Some of the sons of the Kohathite were over the bread of the row, to prepare it every sabbath.
Levites “of the sons of the Kohathites (הַקְּהָתִים) and of the sons of the Korahites” rise to praise Yahweh with a loud voice.
Mahath and Joel “of the sons of the Kohathite” among the Levites who cleanse the house under Hezekiah.
Zechariah and Meshullam of the sons of the Kohathites oversee the work of repair under Josiah.

evidence.locator: קְהָתִי → κααθ ×12, κααθι ×2, κααθίτης ×1 (MACULA alignment); Num.10.21, הַקְּהָתִים → κααθ; Num.26.57, הַקְּהָתִי → κααθι

parallels.note: The Gershonite clan, named beside the Kohathite in the counts and the duties of the Levites.
The Merarite clan, the third of Levi’s sons’ clans, named with the Kohathite.

phrases.gloss: the sons of the Kohathite, the Kohathites

cognates.gloss: (verb) obey; order, command; (noun) obedience; authority, command
cognates.note: Sabaean: the verb wqh “obey (one)” and “order, command”, as “all who obeyed him” and “which the god commanded”; its noun drops the first letter, qh or qht, “obedience; authority, command”, the two senses often not to be told apart (“by command of the king”; “they declared their obedience”). The noun qht has the same three letters as קְהָת, and Hebrew has the root in יִקְּהָה “obedience” (Gen 49:10; Pro 30:17). It bears only on what the name may mean, not on the gentilic’s sense.

evidence.locator: pp. 144–145, WQH (verb obey, order, command; nouns qh, qht obedience, authority, command)

doctrine.statement: The Kohathites were given the most holy things to carry (Num 4:4), but only after Aaron and his sons had covered them; they were to carry them on the shoulder with poles and “not touch the holy things and die”, nor “go in to see the holy things as they are covered, and die” (Num 4:15, 19–20), and so they were given no wagons (Num 7:9). Aaron and his sons were charged to set each man to his burden so that “the tribe of the clans of the Kohathite” would not be cut off (Num 4:17–19). When the ark was later set on a new cart and Uzzah put out his hand to it, he died (2Sa 6:3, 6–7), and David afterward said that none but the Levites should carry the ark, since Yahweh had broken out on them “because we did not seek him according to the ordinance”, and the Levites carried it on their shoulders with the poles “as Moses commanded according to the word of Yahweh” (1Ch 15:2, 13–15). From the verses: nearness to Yahweh’s holy things was by the way he appointed, and even those chosen to bear them lived only by keeping that way.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13. Root key: the database files קְהָת (s.ap.ai) and קְהָתִי (s.ap.aj) under root קהל, but only because BDB prints them after קהל in alphabetical order with no derivation; ל and ת do not interchange, so no tie to קהל “assemble” is claimed and the entry takes the name’s own consonants קהת. The root forms no other word in scripture, so the entry holds the gentilic קְהָתִי (s.ap.aj) as its one word, and the name קְהָת (s.ap.ai) is in names/kohath.json. This differs from names/gershon.json and names/merari.json, which claim their gentilics; if the reviewer wants the same here, the gentilic would move to the name and this entry would need another word. The possible link to יקה “obey” (יִקְּהָה, j.da.ab, Gen 49:10; Pro 30:17) rests on Sabaean wqh with its noun qht (Biella pp. 144–145, checked in the scan’s OCR text); יִקְּהָה is left to a future יקה entry and not claimed here. Not found: Lane has no article وقه (its last volume is abridged at و); BDB’s Arabic waqiha “obey” and Akkadian âḳâ are therefore not cited. Septuagint renders the gentilic as indeclinable Κααθ; the New Testament never names Kohath, so no Greek verse is cited.
